raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Port of DBO fix #51402 to the V2 runner. The scheduler can admit a request on a prefix cache hit against blocks another request in the same batch is only filling in this step. Run whole, every layer's KV write precedes any read; split by DBO, a reader in the first microbatch can attend over blocks the writer in the second has not written yet.

V2 keeps its block tables on the GPU only, so BlockTables gains an optional host mirror, enabled when microbatching is configured. Readers are limited to requests admitted this step (V2 receives resumed requests as new ones), which also covers the one-token query over a fully cached prompt that V1's query-length filter skips. DCP-sharded groups are indexed by virtual block.

Also parametrize tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py over both model runners, setting VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER explicitly since DBO still defaults to V1.

Looks like v1 does not have this problem as the requests are condensed so that rows 0..num_reqs-1 are the current batch, in batch order.  Hence one can do  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0f0bc4dbb1177d3391dfb6f3dbd336f226315106/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L3700

which is actually a more efficient slice.

Maybe it is worth to rewrite for efficiency as follows:

-            axis=1,
-        )[columns < stop[:, None]]
+        written = table[
+            idx_mapping_np[:, None], np.minimum(columns, table.shape[1] - 1)

     assert desc.cg_mode == CUDAGraphMode.NONE
     assert desc.num_ubatches == 2
     assert dp_sync_state is not None and dp_sync_state.eager
+
+
+def _splits_prefix(
+    rows: list[list[int]],
+    num_computed: list[int],
+    num_scheduled: list[int],
+    readers: list[int],
+    tokens_per_entry: int = 4,
+) -> bool:
+    width = max(len(row) for row in rows)
+    table = np.zeros((len(rows), width), dtype=np.int32)
+    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
+        table[i, : len(row)] = row
+    # Request-state row i holds request "i"; only readers count as admitted.
+    scheduler_output = SimpleNamespace(
+        scheduled_new_reqs=[
+            SimpleNamespace(req_id=str(i), num_computed_tokens=num_computed[i])
+            for i in readers
+        ]
+    )
+    batch_req_state = SimpleNamespace(
+        idx_mapping_np=np.arange(len(rows), dtype=np.intp),
+        num_scheduled_tokens=np.array(num_scheduled, dtype=np.int32),
+    )
+    req_states = SimpleNamespace(
+        req_id_to_index={str(i): i for i in range(len(rows))},
+        num_computed_tokens_np=np.array(num_computed, dtype=np.int32),
+    )
+    block_tables = SimpleNamespace(
+        block_tables_np=[table], tokens_per_entry=[tokens_per_entry]
+    )
+    return splits_prefix_from_writer(
+        cast(Any, scheduler_output),
+        cast(Any, batch_req_state),
+        cast(Any, req_states),
+        cast(Any, block_tables),
+    )
+
+
+def test_prefix_hit_on_blocks_written_this_step_vetoes_microbatching():
+    # Request 0 fills blocks 10 and 11 this step; request 1 was admitted on a
+    # prefix cache hit against both. Split, request 1 could read them first.
+    assert _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[10, 11], [10, 11, 20]],
+        num_computed=[0, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[8, 3],
+        readers=[1],
+    )
+    # A one-token query over a fully cached prompt still reads the prefix.
+    assert _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[10, 11], [10, 11, 20]],
+        num_computed=[0, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[8, 1],
+        readers=[1],
+    )
+
+
+def test_prefix_hit_on_blocks_written_earlier_allows_microbatching():
+    # Request 0 filled blocks 10 and 11 in an earlier step and writes only
+    # block 12 now.
+    assert not _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[10, 11, 12], [10, 11, 20]],
+        num_computed=[8, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[1, 3],
+        readers=[1],
+    )
+    # No request was admitted on a hit.
+    assert not _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[10, 11], [10, 11, 20]],
+        num_computed=[0, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[8, 3],
+        readers=[],
+    )
+
+
+def test_prefix_hit_check_ignores_the_null_block():
+    # Sliding-window entries that fell out of the window point at block 0,
+    # which a writer's redirected (e.g. EPLB warmup) writes may also target.
+    assert not _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[0, 0], [0, 11, 20]],
+        num_computed=[0, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[8, 3],
+        readers=[1],
+    )
+
+
+def test_prefix_hit_check_uses_dcp_virtual_blocks():
+    # With DCP, one entry covers block_size * dcp_size tokens: request 0 fills
+    # only entry 0 (block 10), which request 1 hits as its whole first entry.
+    assert _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[10], [10, 20]],
+        num_computed=[0, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[8, 3],
+        readers=[1],
+        tokens_per_entry=8,
+    )
+    assert not _splits_prefix(
+        rows=[[10, 11], [12, 20]],
+        num_computed=[0, 8],
+        num_scheduled=[8, 3],
+        readers=[1],
+        tokens_per_entry=8,
+    )
